en.headline: Rain and internet outages mark first day of Hong Kong robot convenience stores
en.dek: Three Galbot Stores staffed by humanoid robots opened in Hung Hom, Wan Chai and Kai Tak on Tuesday, drawing visitors despite technical hiccups and wet weather.
body: Hong Kong’s first fully automated convenience stores operated by humanoid robots began trading on Tuesday, but heavy rain and intermittent internet outages affected the outdoor outlets in Hung Hom and Wan Chai.

The three Galbot Stores, run by mainland firm Galbot, feature the wheeled humanoid robot manager known as Xiao Gai. Customers place orders on a screen, pay by card or mainland mobile wallets, and receive items retrieved by the robot. The indoor unit at Kai Tak Sports Park operated more smoothly.

Visitors photographed the Hung Hom waterfront store and chatted with the robot, which greeted passers-by in Cantonese. Galbot, backed by the Hong Kong Investment Corporation, plans further outlets in the city after operating about 200 stores across 50 mainland cities.
Financial Secretary Paul Chan attended a launch ceremony on Monday and said Hong Kong could serve as an application scenario, research hub and capital platform for embodied AI robotics.

zh.headline: 全港首批機械人便利店首日遇雨及網絡故障
zh.dek: 銀河通用三間由人形機械人管理的Galbot Store周二於紅磡、灣仔及啟德開業，戶外店受大雨及網絡不穩影響，仍吸引市民到訪。
body: 本港首批全自主機械人便利店周二正式開業，紅磡及灣仔兩間戶外店因大雨及間歇網絡故障受影響，啟德體育園室內店則較暢順。
三間Galbot Store由內地企業銀河通用營運，店長為輪式人形機械人「小蓋」。顧客於螢幕落單，以信用卡或內地電子錢包付款後，由機械人取貨交收。
不少市民在紅磡新海濱店拍照及與機械人對話，機械人以粵語招呼途人。銀河通用獲港投公司支持，內地已有約200間店，計劃在港增設更多分店。
財政司司長陳茂波周一出席啟動禮，指香港可在具身智能機械人領域發揮應用場景、研發生態及資本鏈的獨特角色。
